bounded_status_check: No vetted per-feed success/status accessor exists in the inspected watcher interface; no logs, RSS, or state were reread for this code diagnosis.
evidence: Each daemon loop loads config, then state, then calls poll_once, then sleeps for configured interval (lines 909–918).

Per feed, exceptions from feedparser.parse are logged and skipped; otherwise the daemon orders entries newest-first, applies max_entries_per_feed, and computes SHA-1 of id/guid/link/title (lines 646–649, 744–751).

For each unrecognized ID, seen.add(eid) happens before title dedup and tier1/tier2 keyword matching; no keyword means no alert, but the ID remains in seen and is saved after the cycle (lines 752–755, 761–774, 861–864).

The built-in status command reports PID, total seen-ID count and last cron trigger only; it has no per-feed last-success/error record (lines 935–945). Feed parse exceptions are logged at lines 745–749; successful empty results have no per-feed marker.
inference: Absence of Kimi/Moonshot keywords cannot itself explain missing IDs once the configured feed was fetched and those entries fell within its newest-N cap; keyword filtering occurs after seen-ID insertion.

The seven IDs could remain unseen if the new config had not yet been loaded for a poll, feed retrieval/parsing failed or returned no entries, or the current RSS variant/cap no longer included them. This offline check cannot distinguish these causes.
A state-file mtime after config mtime does not establish that the daemon loaded that config: an in-flight cycle could have loaded the prior config and saved state afterward.
